heterogeneous_fp16.mapping: NPU ViT+projector + CPU action encoder + NPU terminal predictor+pred_proj

notes: Complete-solve stage values are means of five repeated requests.
After matching PyTorch workers to the four pinned CPU cores, the heterogeneous action encoder is only 0.17% slower, within measurement noise.

The earlier 4.90% gap was a cross-process benchmark artifact amplified by eight PyTorch workers competing on four pinned cores; controlled tests measured +0.10% for NumPy copies and +0.17% for a real NPU predictor.
The Action Encoder conversion issue was isolated to a Transpose/Reshape plus Linear attention-output fusion and fixed with an equivalent 1x1 Conv.
Keeping 300 CEM candidates fixed while changing only RKNN micro-batch preserves numerical agreement; batch 300 is fastest in the measured sweep.
A full-NPU result is excluded because the accurate NPU Action Encoder is 2.02x slower than the tuned four-core CPU implementation.
Current and goal images are encoded once per planning request, outside the 30-iteration CEM loop.
The action-prefix encoder consumes all five blocks and returns only the terminal prefix token.
The fused NPU graph contains the terminal predictor and pred_proj.
